review_notes: I read all of LimitActions.lean. I also read the definitions it depends on: LimitLaws and exists_limitLaws in CriticalLimits.lean, the ArrayActions.lean extension and translation lemmas, and scaleLaw_translate in ScaleLaws.lean. The hypotheses are satisfiable. LimitLaws is shown to be nonempty by exists_limitLaws, and the invariance hypothesis hμ is realised eventually by multiLaw_translate_eventually and terminalLaw_translate_eventually. arrayTestExtend sets the extension to zero on the affine locus, and integral_arrayTestExtend ties it to nonaffinePart. That makes the translation and dilation compatibility lemmas faithful. The final statements say that the limit measures on the non-affine arrays are invariant under every dyadic translation, and they do not collapse to a trivial claim. I did not check the full definitions of multiLaw or terminalLaw. In particular I did not verify that the limit measures are nonzero. That question belongs to other files and not to the statements here.
